$comment: Test vectors for docs/spec/waterfall-terms.md. Every vector is run against the engine by lib/accounting/waterfall-spec.test.ts, so this file and the code cannot disagree. Money is in currency units, rounded to cents; rates are fractions (0.2 = 20%). Section names are the engine functions each vector exercises.

runWaterfall.description: A distribution smaller than unreturned capital is all return of capital.
Capital comes back first, then the preferred return; nothing is left for the catch-up.
All four tiers: 1000 capital, 80 pref, 20 catch-up (GP reaches 20% of 100), remainder 80/20. GP ends with 20% of the 500 profit.
An 80% catch-up rate: 25 of flow gives the GP its full catch-up of 20 (20% of the 80 pref plus the catch-up) and the LPs 5. The split takes the rest (spec 3.2).
An 80% catch-up rate the distribution does not fill: 15 of flow gives the GP 12 and the LPs 3, the literal reading of the catch-up rate (spec 3.2).
catchUpRate 0: there is no catch-up tier; after the pref the remainder splits at the carry rate.
State carries over: capital and pref already paid, GP 10 of 20 caught up. The catch-up finishes, the rest splits.
carryRate 0: no catch-up tier and the split gives the GP nothing.
preferredTarget 0 (how straight carry runs): no pref, no catch-up, capital then the split.
Every tier is rounded to cents; the GP's split share is rounded and the LP takes the rest.
The distributable itself is rounded to cents first.
25% carry at fund scale: the catch-up target 0.25 x 320000 / 0.75 rounds to 106666.67.

The hurdle grew after the fund had already reached the split. 40 more pref makes a full catch-up 30 (20% of 120 + 30), of which the GP already has 20 from its catch-up; split carry does not count. It catches up 10, then the split resumes (spec 3.2).
A 10% catch-up rate on 20% carry: the GP still gets its full catch-up of 20, but at 10% of each dollar it takes 200 of flow, 180 of it to the LPs. The split takes the rest (spec 3.2).
A catch-up sized at half a full one: the GP catches up 10 rather than 20 (half of 20% of the 80 pref plus a full catch-up), then the split takes the rest (spec 3.2).

A half-size first catch-up (12.50 on the 100 pref), 20% until the LPs have 2.5x, then a 100% catch-up measured on the split: the GP is owed 30% of the 1,750 the 20% split paid less its 350 from it, 175, then 30% on the rest (spec 3.3).

preferredTarget.description: 730 days is exactly 2 years under ACTUAL/365: 1000 x (1.08^2 - 1).
2024 has 366 days, so a calendar year is 366/365 years.
Each contribution accrues from its own date; one on or after asOf accrues nothing; non-positive amounts are ignored.
On the contributed base the hurdle accrues on gross contributions; capital already returned keeps accruing (spec 5).
Unreturned base, compounding: 80 of pref is paid after a year, so the second year accrues on the 1,000 of capital alone. 160, against 166.40 on the contributed base (spec 5).
Unreturned base, compounding: all capital comes back after a year, so only the 80 of unpaid pref keeps compounding (spec 5).
Unreturned base, simple: half the capital comes back after a year and the second year accrues on the other half; unpaid pref never accrues (spec 5).

carryTarget.description: Straight with a loss accrues nothing.
European: the waterfall on a hypothetical liquidation (NAV + distributed) from a clean state, pref accrued to asOf.
Liquidation value inside the hurdle: no carry.
American accrues exactly the European target (spec 4.3).
Unreturned base at the close: the 1,000 already distributed returned all capital a year in, so the hurdle is 86.40, not 166.40, and the GP catches up on the 13.60 left above it (spec 4.3, 5).
The same books on the contributed base: the hurdle is 166.40, the 100 of profit does not clear it, and there is no carry (spec 5).

Whole fund: LP A puts in 1,000 on 2020-01-01 and LP B 1,000 on 2023-01-01; 8% compounding pref, 20% carry, full catch-up, gross NAV 3,000 at 2025-01-01. One waterfall on the pooled capital and hurdle gives the GP 200.

The same books per LP: the 3,000 is divided 1,500 each by contributions. LP A is 5 years in (pref 469.95), so only 30.05 is left for the catch-up; LP B is 2 years in (pref 166.65), clears its catch-up and pays 58.34 of split. 130.05 in total, charged 30.05 and 100.

Per LP, hurdle on unreturned capital, both LPs in 1,000 on 2020-01-01. 1,000 went out on 2022-01-01 but not by the division: LP A took 800 and LP B 200. Each LP's hurdle is replayed from what it actually received, so LP A's stops accruing on the 800 returned. Gross NAV 1,400 is divided 700 each: LP A's 1,500 clears its smaller hurdle and the GP takes 100 (30.05 on a contributed base); LP B's 900 doesn't return its capital.

splitDistribution.description: A prior 500 (all capital) is replayed first; this 1000 then finishes capital, pays the 2-year pref on the 1000 contributed, catches up and splits. LP lines follow contributed capital.
American terms with no realized deals supplied: the split falls back to the whole-fund waterfall, with a warning (spec 4.3).
Straight: no hurdle and no catch-up, capital then the split.
The GP take splits across recipients by pct; the last absorbs the rounding cent.
kind none: pro-rata by capital balance across every partner, method pro_rata.
The replay-then-split books on the unreturned base: the prior 500 returned half the capital, so the second year accrues on 500 plus the unpaid first-year pref (spec 5).

American: a 400 deal sells for 1,000 after a 200 deal was written off. The capital tier is the 600 in realized deals, not the 1,000 contributed, so the GP is paid carry now: 20% of the 400 of realized profit (spec 4.3).
The carryTarget books distributed in full per LP: 1,500 to each LP's own tiers. The GP takes 30.05 from LP A and 100 from LP B, 130.05 in all (200 on the whole fund).

Per LP, no pref, both LPs in 1,000 on 2020-01-01. On 2022-01-01 LP A took 900 and LP B 100 of a 1,000 distribution, with no carry. The replay reads those receipts, so of this 2,000 (1,000 each by contributions) LP A has 100 of capital left and pays carry on 900, LP B has 900 left and pays carry on 100. Re-dividing the prior would have returned 500 each.

dealByDealCarry.description: A winner pays carry on its gain over cost plus its share of expenses; a loser pays nothing and does not offset.
